# Traitors
[color=#999999][italic]"WHISKEY. ECHO. WHISKEY. LIMA. ALPHA. DELTA. AGENT, YOU HAVE BEEN ACTIVATED."[/italic][/color]
Traitors are a shadowy organization employed by the [color=#ff0000]Syndicate.[/color]
Unlike other servers, Traitors on Ephemeral Space are a team antagonist--closer to a mix of Traitors and Nuclear Operatives.
[bold][color=yellow]Important information for new players:[/bold][/color] - Take in as much information here as you need. There's no need to rush when reading this guidebook page. Traitors typically have an easier time as the round goes on and conflict brews without them, so you'll probably be doing yourself a favor by waiting a bit, anyways. - Don't be afraid of letting your team down. No individual traitor is expected to be perfect; it's rather common for even experienced agents to slip up and die quickly. Your team will likely help pick up the slack if you fail. Even if you are the last traitor and lose, there's no penalty for failure, other tham the bitter taste of defeat. - You can get away with more then you think. Most illicit actions have reasonable plausible deniability (see [italic]Feigning as Other Secret Identities & Claims[/italic] section below.) You'll need to break in to places and take risky actions to complete your objectives. This can be scary, but it's worth trying, even if it might result in death. - If someone asks you what your secret identity is, and you aren't sure what to say / don't know what secret identities exist, [bold]claim to be a Vandal.[/bold] This isn't the perfect option in every situation, but it will save you if you have no other alibi, since vandals are the only other secret identity that can sabotage machines.
## Gear All traitors start with a [bold]hidden cache[/bold] in maintenance that only they can retrieve. By going to the coordinates / area listed in the character menu and clicking the action, a duffel bag will drop out of the ceiling, containing several items related to the traitor's secret identity.
While somewhat dangerous to carry, these are invaluable tools for completing your objectives, and you should definitely try to pick them up at some point during the round. Their reward far outweighs their potential risk.
Other (non-traitor) players can also get traitor gear through the [textlink="Ex-Syndie" link="ExSyndie"] secret identity modifier, so keep that in mind. Holding a traitor kit is usually not an instant out because of this, but will still end up increasing your suspicion levels to others.
## Objectives All traitors on the team share the same objectives, and must work together to complete them. To succeed, they must detonate the nuke inside of the station's vault.
Objectives come in phases. To detonate the nuke, all security override terminals must be hacked, and to hack the terminals, all basic objectives must be completed.
Currently, there are 7 different possible basic traitor objectives that be chosen, of 3 different categories:
### Basic Objectives
[bold]Kill Random[/bold]
You've been assigned to kill someone on the station. This can select [italic]anyone who is not a part of the traitor organization,[/italic] including friendly [textlink="Sympathizers." link="Sympathizer"]
[bold]Sabotage[/bold]
You need to sabotage the machine your objective tells you to. You can do this by opening up the context menu on them and selecting "sabotage." Doing this causes adverse effects that typically alert people to your presence.
Every machine has a different effect when sabotaged. For example, telecomms will replace the majority of messages with static, and the communications computer will send a garbled announcement.
[bold]Bug APC[/bold]
You need to apply a bug to any APC inside of a randomly-selected department. Like sabotaging, you perform this through opening up the context menu on an applicable apc and clicking "sabotage." Once the bug is planted, it will take a few minutes to complete the objective. It can be removed by anyone, so make sure you place it in a secure location!
Once the objective is complete, the APC bug will dissapear, and the affected department will have the [italic]grey tide virus[/italic] event triggered inside of it.
Importantly, unlike Sabotage, [bold]Bug APC is never a vandal objective. It is strictly traitor-exclusive, and getting caught outs you as such.[/bold] Avoid getting caught in the act at all costs - the crew is not likely to take very kindly to seeing you do this.
## Security Override Terminals
When all basic objectives are done, the security override terminals can be compromised by opening their UI and clicking "hack." Once all three terminals are compromised, the nuke codes will appear, enabling the detonation of the nuke, provided the nuclear authentication disk is also obtained.
After seeing the codes appear, it's common practice to say them in the traitor radio channel so they can be utilized by other teammates & remembered for later, if things go south.
The three terminals are located in [bold]the HoP's secure room (the leftmost airlock in the HOP's room,) the captain's office (inside of the bridge,) and secure tech storage (below tool storage.)[/bold]
## Nuke
The final step in the Syndicate's plan. While then nuke codes are a required component of arming the nuke, it also needs the nuclear authentication disk. It can be located by looking at the sercurity override terminal's UI, or by using a nuke disk pinpointer.
The captain starts with a nuke disk pinpointer and the nuke disk in their locker. If they so choose, these can be given away to anyone, but typically, the captain carries both.
To obtain it, you will likely need to kill the captain or whoever is holding the disk, unless it's just sitting somewhere.
After the nuke is armed, a 60 second countdown that alerts all crew will begin. This is still enough time for a powerful-enough crew to disarm, so be careful - you may want to secure the area around the vault or pick other players off before activating the detonation sequence, to ensure your safety.
## Feigning as Other Secret Identites & Claims People will often ask what your secret identity is when you act suspiciously, which you will probably doing a lot of as traitor. It's also pretty likely that, at some point, you will get caught in the act. While the best possible secret identity to claim depends on the situation, there are a lot of generally useful ones:
- [textlink="Vandal" link="Vandal"]: Mentioned in the new player section above for a good reason. The vandal's only goal is to sabotage machines, like a traitor. This makes them a good mostly-futureproof-cover, and a perfect alibi for if you get caught sabotaging a machine. This may backfire if your cache's gear is found, though - someone with traitor items, traitorous behavior, [italic]and[/italic] traitor gear is more likely then not to be seen a traitor! - [textlink="Stalker" link="Stalker"]: This secret identity must pick 5 other players using an action, and ensuring that 2 of them are alive and 3 of them are dead by the end of the round. This can work as good cover for excusing allowing someone to die, or as an alibi when you get caught murdering someone. Just be aware that people aren't generally receptive to mass-murder, even if someone is actually crew. - [textlink="Avenger" link="Avenger"]: If their target dies, this secret identity must kill the player who killed their protect target. This can work fairly well if you are keeping track of who has died and who killed who - often times, crew will not get in the way of a determined avenger. - [textlink="Tragedian" link="Tragedian"]: A secret identity that must put on a performance that embodies a certain theme, then die. This can be risky, since the crew may want to let the tragedian die in some situations. However, there is no downside to claiming this if you are not caught doing any machine sabotage or APC bugging, and it may let you get off scott-free if you can manage to feign a performance with a defined theme - people generally enjoy going along with the tragedian, if they know they exist.
Additionally it should be stated that, above all else, actions speak louder than words. If you act like a traitor and are caught with traitor gear, it's likely you will be executed on the spot, regardless of whatever secret identity you claim to be. This is inversely true - if you commit to pretending to be a certain secret identity from the start of the round, it's significantly more likely people will believe you, provided your act doesn't seem suspicious.
## General Tips and Strategy - It's extremely effective to wait for when people are distracted to sabotage. Alternatively, you can cause a distraction yourself (try spacing, substation destruction in an important location, or firebombs.) - Try to appear as a normal member of the crew by helping others & doing your job where possible. This will make you a lot more credible if you ever find yourself in a sticky situation (such as being found with traitor items, or caught sabotaging a machine.) The more suspicious actions you get found doing, the more likely people are to think you're a traitor. - Talking / lying your way out of situations instead of initiating combat when pressured is often useful. Engaging in combat in these situations makes you seem like an [italic]extremely obvious[/italic] traitor; it is not recommended to do unless you have absolutely no other choice.
